objective: Make large-corpus matter discovery complete and resumable before legal candidate selection, while keeping tool output bounded.

changes.failure_pattern: Broad corpus listings and searches silently stopped at fixed prefixes, which were then treated as exhaustive candidate inventories.
changes.mechanism: Return deterministic bounded pages with total, truncation, and continuation metadata; expose direct-directory enumeration so every matter can enter the census without a giant context dump.
changes.rationale: The earliest recurrent defect was success-shaped partial output from discovery tools, so the strongest reusable fix belongs in the tool implementation rather than relying only on model caution.

changes.failure_pattern: Agents received no indication that result caps required continuation and treated binary grep no-matches as evidence of absence.
changes.mechanism: Describe pagination preconditions and output fields beside the schemas, require continuation while truncated, and distinguish decoded text search from format-aware Office-document reading.
changes.rationale: The model must correctly interpret the new structured page metadata and avoid applying plain-text search semantics to binary matter documents.

changes.failure_pattern: Across matters, agents narrowed from visible hits before forming a complete candidate denominator and lost discovered candidates during follow-up.
changes.mechanism: Require a paginated matter census, concise qualification ledger, bounded recovery from timeouts, primary/status evidence review, and final reconciliation for corpus-wide or superlative requests, while exempting explicitly named-file tasks.
changes.rationale: Tool completeness removes silent clipping, but the agent still needs an operational state transition from census to qualification to drafting so complete pages become a maintained legal-review denominator.

validation: Synthetic multi-page glob and grep smoke tests
